message.reasoning_content:
We need to determine appropriate criminal charge(s) based on facts. The facts: On March 26, 2017, at 6am, defendant Zhang stole a bag from victim Lin, containing two phones and cash 545 RMB. The phones: Samsung GT-I9168I (value 250) and Huawei Honor 6 (value 500). Cash 545. After, Samsung phone and 500 RMB were recovered. The defendant was arrested March 27. On April 3, family repaid 545 RMB. All stolen items and money returned to victim.

Thus the crime is robbery? Actually "抢夺" is theft by force? In Chinese criminal law, "抢夺" (robbery) is taking property by force or threat, but "抢夺" is a specific crime: "抢夺罪" (robbery by snatching). The facts: "趁被害人不备，抢夺走林的1个包". That is snatching. So the charge is "抢夺". Also maybe "盗窃"? But the act is with force? The phrase "抢夺" is used in many examples for similar facts. So the appropriate charge: 抢夺.

Check if any other charges: The defendant returned the money and items, but still the crime is completed. No other crimes like "非法占有" is part of robbery. So only one charge.

Thus answer: [罪名]抢夺<eoa>
